notation.receiver_coordinate: X=U/V with U,V positive coprime integers

unique_primitive_boundary.statement: among positive coprime integer pairs (U,V), Lminus=0 iff U=(P/h)^2 and V=(M/h)^2
unique_primitive_boundary.proof: write P=hP0 and M=hM0 with gcd(|P0|,|M0|)=1. Lminus=0 gives M0^2 U=P0^2 V. Coprimality forces P0^2|U and M0^2|V; after substitution and gcd(U,V)=1 the common multiplier is 1. The converse is immediate.
unique_primitive_boundary.squareclass_tuple: exactly the hostile-audited AY tuple A=B=D=1, C=odd_sf(D0), eta=sign(D0), f=1, e=(1+v2(D0)) mod2

correct_open_refinement.AY_specialization: for A=B=1 the excluded projective ratios are u:v=+/-P:M; the positive primitive U:V boundary is unique
correct_open_refinement.reason: an outer squareclass tuple is a family of coordinate solutions, not a single point. The existence of one boundary realization does not prove that every realization of that tuple lies on the boundary.

tunnell_limit.consequence: Tunnell equality cannot distinguish the AY X=K boundary realization from any hypothetical nonboundary realization in the same squareclass tuple
tunnell_limit.safe_conclusion: the AW Tunnell outer sieve may be refined only by adding a coordinate-level open condition; deleting the AY tuple itself would be unsound without a complete rational-point classification of that branch
